title: Sinusoidal Waveform Anatomy
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: sinusoidal waveform
amplitude
frequency
period
phase
RMS value
AC signals
electrical engineering
description: Interactive MicroSim that labels the peak, peak-to-peak, RMS level, period, zero crossings and phase shift of a sinusoidal voltage v(t) = Vm sin(2*pi*f*t + phi) while sliders change amplitude, frequency and phase on fixed axes.

learningObjectives: Explain the relationship between sinusoidal parameters (amplitude, frequency, phase) and the resulting waveform shape

controls.label: RMS Level
controls.description: Show or hide the RMS level line

controls.label: Reference
controls.description: Switch between the sine form and the cosine form

assumptions: Ideal sinusoid with no DC offset, noise or distortion

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict-observe-explain using sliders on fixed axes
keyQuestions: What changes on the screen when the amplitude doubles? When the frequency doubles?
Why does a positive phase angle move the waveform to the left?
Why is the RMS level always about 71% of the peak?
commonMisconceptions: A positive phase shift moves the waveform to the right (later in time)
RMS is the same as the average value of the waveform
assessmentOpportunities: Compute Vrms, Vpp, omega and T by hand for chosen slider settings and compare with the labels
